title: M4Bench: Evaluating Procedural Specification for Clinical EHR Derivation Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.37459v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Clinical research over electronic health records depends on derived variables whose definitions sit outside the schema, in item codes, time windows, missingness rules, and output-grain choices that change cohorts and downstream conclusions. We introduce M4Bench, 28 clinical derivation tasks across 15 task families on MIMIC-IV and eICU, to test whether AI coding agents can reproduce such derivations and how clinician-reviewed agent skills change their results. Its controls decompose the value of skills into specification completeness, delivery format, and schema familiarity. In a Docker-isolated Codex campaign (GPT 5.4 Mini and GPT 5.5), skills raise reward by 0.136 over the no-skill baseline, with 26 of 28 tasks improving. Specification completeness accounts for most of this gain: on an eight-task control subset, an operational spec alone raises reward by 0.162, and skills add only 0.024 on top, indistinguishable from zero. translated_title: M4Bench：面向临床电子健康记录推导智能体的程序性规范评估
translated_abstract: 基于电子健康记录的临床研究依赖于派生变量，其定义存在于数据库模式之外，体现在项目编码、时间窗口、缺失值规则和输出粒度选择上，而这些选择会改变队列构成和下游研究结论。我们提出M4Bench，这是一个基于MIMIC-IV和eICU的基准，包含涵盖15个任务族的28个临床推导任务，用于测试AI编程智能体能否复现此类推导，以及经临床医生审查的智能体技能如何改变其结果。该基准的对照设计将技能的价值分解为规范完整性、交付格式和模式熟悉度三个部分。在一项Docker隔离的Codex实验（使用GPT 5.4 Mini和GPT 5.5）中，技能相比无技能基线将奖励提升了0.136，28个任务中有26个得到改善。规范完整性贡献了大部分收益：在一个八任务对照子集上，仅操作性规范就能将奖励提升0.162，而技能在此基础上仅额外增加0.024，与零无显著差异。
tldr: M4Bench基准通过28个临床EHR推导任务发现，AI编程智能体的性能提升主要来自完整的操作性规范，而非额外的技能包。
en_tdlr: M4Bench shows that performance gains of AI coding agents on 28 clinical EHR derivation tasks stem mainly from complete operational specifications rather than additional agent skills.
